main_text.p: jusvis temporis, dicitur litera vel diphthongus ante finalem syllabam.
Si thematis impuri ultima syllaba geminam consonam habeat, prior sola est figurativa: ut in πλάσσω fingo, ψάλλω fidibus cano, τέμνω seco, πίπτω pario, τύπτω verbero.

Conjugatio Latina, temporibus finitis & infinitis, in eadem forma quadruplex est, amare, flere, petere, audire: at Græca conjugatio omnium unius formæ verborum, personarum finibus una est, sicut Herodianus grammaticus recte monuit: nec in derivatis circumflexis, vel in μι, anomalia paucorum temporum aliam significationem verbi, vel aliam conjugationis speciem facit, cum reliqua tempora consentiant, & conjugandis circumflexis necesse sit etiam barytona conjugari: ut tam temere baryto-

page.notes: Greek words in the lines "ut in ... fingo" are printed in Greek letters; transcribed as best read. Some Greek glyphs are uncertain and may need checking. Catchword "baryto-" is part of the text line and is kept in the paragraph.
